claims.text: The target alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
The initial oxygen content exceeds the oxygen solubility limit of the beta phase.
Heating the hydride-containing precursor releases hydrogen and leaves metal available for alloying.
A 1100°C stage provides effective dehydrogenation and activates the Zr getter.
Dispersed metallic Zr scavenges oxygen by forming stable ZrO2.
Zr scavenging lowers oxygen activity or dissolved oxygen below the threshold for alpha-HCP nucleation.
Dissolved oxygen is an alpha-phase stabilizer in HfNbTaTiZr.
The ideal configurational entropy of an equiatomic five-component alloy is ΔSmix = Rln5.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the disordered BCC phase in equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Quenching faster than 100 K/s suppresses diffusion-controlled transformation of high-temperature beta-BCC into alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC.
Rapid quenching from 1350°C traps metastable single-phase beta-BCC HfNbTaTiZr.
The rapidly quenched material will have a grain size below 5 µm.
The proposed process will produce a density above 98%.
The getter-assisted rapidly quenched material will contain no detectable alpha-HCP or alpha-Ti.
Omitting the Zr getter will permit alpha-phase precipitation.
Slow furnace cooling will produce an alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC or alpha-HCP plus beta-BCC microstructure.
Omitting the getter or cooling slowly will produce coarser grains than getter-assisted rapid quenching.
Oxygen-induced phase separation will reduce ductility.
The resulting refractory BCC alloy will exhibit limited ductility.
Successful suppression of alpha phases requires getter capacity in stoichiometric excess of the total oxygen inventory and a cooling rate above a composition-specific critical value.

contradictions.description: The getter is described as Zr powder homogeneously mixed into the precursor and as forming stable ZrO2, yet the outcome is described as a single-phase beta-BCC solid solution. Unless the getter or its oxide is removed, segregated outside the analyzed material, or excluded from phase accounting, ZrO2 would constitute an additional phase.

The alloy is specified as equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, but additional Zr getter is homogeneously mixed in stoichiometric excess without accounting for its effect on alloy composition. Any unoxidized getter would make the metallic composition Zr-rich.
